issues.description: Method Farm.singFarmSongVerse(Animal) has inconsistent access modifiers across artifacts. The UML in the problem statement declares singFarmSongVerse(...) as private (Farm class member shows a leading '-' and the UML entry '- singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal):void'), and the template implementation defines a private helper method signature (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)) on the same line. The solution implementation, however, declares the method as protected (protected void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)). This mismatch may confuse students about whether the helper is intended to be strictly internal (private) or intended to be accessible to subclasses/tests (protected).
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one consistent visibility across the exercise materials. Either: (A) Make the solution match the UML/template by changing the solution method signature to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) (preferred if this helper is internal), or (B) update the problem statement UML and the template comments to declare the helper as protected (and, if needed, adjust the template so the parameter is uncommented once Animal exists). Ensure all three artifacts (problem statement, template, solution) use the same access modifier and document the intent in the task description.
